NVIDIA details Flora’s video-annotation pipeline for robot learning

The system segments actions, writes captions and evaluates execution, with throughput reported across 512 GPUs.

Humanoids Daily ↗21 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 2

A public account of the GR00T data engine

NVIDIA researchers introduced Flora publicly on October 20, followed by Humanoids Daily’s report the next day. It prepares human and robot video for GR00T. The Rewarder card dates its model-file release to October 15, so this covers the system overview and performance disclosure rather than claiming every file first appeared today.

Separating intent from outcome

TempSeg divides footage into action intervals, Captioner describes the attempted operation and Rewarder assesses execution quality or success. A failed grasp can therefore retain its intended-action label without treating failure as the goal. Outputs are learning annotations, not motor commands.

Cluster throughput and usage limits

NVIDIA reports annotating 200,000 video hours daily with 512 GB300 GPUs, not collecting that much new robot experience or training time. Captioner and Rewarder cards restrict intended use to noncommercial research and development. Published comparisons show both stronger and weaker results across individual metrics.
